彩.meaning: A cat with long <part>whiskers</part> rolls the <part>dice</part> to pick a paint pot, one for red and six for gold, dips her whiskers in and flicks them across the white hallway. By lunch the walls are a rainbow, and the landlord is furious about her <kanji>coloring</kanji>.
彩.on: She rinses her whiskers in a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der before the next roll.
彩.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeaks a <sound>ro</sound>dent as she paints its tail to match a <sound>do</sound>lphin poster.

屈.meaning: At the castle <part>exit</part>, the guard's <part>flag</part> is too tall for the low door, so every morning it jams and the whole parade backs up. At last the flagpole gives in and folds itself in half to squeeze through. Even wood knows when to <kanji>yield</kanji>.
屈.on: A <sound>coo</sound>t perches on the folded pole and bows to everyone who passes.
屈.kun: Behind it, a <sound>ca</sound>rp ducks low under the door with a string of <sound>ga</sound>rlic on its head.

炎.meaning: A doctor examines a camper's swollen red ankle. It's so hot that a <part>fire</part> is burning on top of it, and a second fire is perched on top of that. 'Classic,' she says, roasting a marshmallow over it. 'Very bad <kanji>inflammation</kanji>.'
炎.on: The ambulance's <sound>en</sound>gine overheats just driving past.
炎.kun: She cooks a <sound>ho</sound>tdog on the flames too, wailing '<sound>No</sound>, <sound>oh</sound> no!' as it chars.

幅.meaning: A greedy bear spots a <part>cookie jar</part> through the kitchen door, but he's too fat to fit. He holds a <part>towel</part> across the doorway to measure it, then across himself, and sighs. The problem is clearly his own <kanji>width</kanji>.
幅.on: So he fishes the jar out through the window with a long <sound>hook</sound>.
幅.kun: He eats the cookies outside his <sound>hu</sound>t, next to the <sound>ba</sound>rbecue, where there are no doors at all.

卒.meaning: After <part>ten</part> long years at clown school, the <part>twins</part> toss their caps in the air, but someone has glued both caps to one saucepan <part>lid</part>, so it clangs back down on both heads at once. Everyone cheers anyway. They <kanji>graduate</kanji>.
卒.on: They collapse on a <sound>so</sound>fa and sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' from all the confetti.
卒.kun: '<sound>So</sound>!' snaps the head clown, cutting the speech dead and shooing them off the stage.

宣.meaning: A chef climbs onto the <part>roof</part> of his diner, holds the world's tallest <part>burger</part> over his head and bellows to the whole street: 'Free fries for anyone who can finish it!' Pigeons gather. He loves to <kanji>proclaim</kanji> things from up there.
宣.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try across the road salutes and asks for extra pickles.
宣.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' shouts a <sound>ta</sound>co seller below, banging a <sound>mu</sound>g on his cart.

繰.meaning: Kids in a <part>treehouse</part> lower a basket on a long <part>thread</part> to the snack shop below, then turn a creaky crank to haul it back up: biscuits, comics, a grumpy cat. Round and round goes the handle. Their whole day is spent <kanji>winding</kanji>.
繰.on: One basket comes back with nothing but a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p from their mum.
繰.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo nests on the crank and pops out every time it turns.

既.meaning: A time-travelling <part>robot</part> walks into a party and finds a note taped to every <part>chair back</part>, in its own handwriting: 'Been here. Ate the cake. Go home.' It sighs a puff of steam. It has done all of this <kanji>previously</kanji>.
既.on: It unlocks its time machine with a big brass <sound>key</sound> and tries again.
既.kun: It lands in a cloud of <sound>soo</sound>t on the host's <sound>de</sound>sk, too late once more.

抑.meaning: A grumpy postmaster won't allow giggling in the queue. When a laugh bubbles up, he slams his rubber <part>stamp</part> down on it, and if it keeps coming he drops an iron <part>anchor</part> on top. By noon the room is silent. He'll <kanji>repress</kanji> every smile.
抑.on: Only a drip of egg <sound>yolk</sound> from his own sandwich makes his lip twitch.
抑.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' he says, and presses a wriggling <sound>sa</sound>rdine flat under the anchor too.

耐.meaning: A wizard's <part>beard</part> is so long that the castle gardener uses it as a putting green, tapping balls across it with a <part>golf club</part>. Every swing tugs at his chin, but he hasn't blinked in three hundred years. He's the most <kanji>enduring</kanji> wizard alive.
耐.on: He keeps the end tidy with a striped <sound>tie</sound> knotted round it.
耐.kun: At night he soaks it in a <sound>tu</sound>b and still doesn't complain.

概.meaning: An artist was asked to paint a forest, but he <part>previously</part> spent all his paint on his front door. So he traces round one <part>tree</part> with a pencil, labels it 'forest, roughly' and hands it in. The judges squint at the thin line. It's only an <kanji>outline</kanji>.
概.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads the judges round the pencil tree as if it were real.
概.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>... <sound>oh</sound>,' sighs a <sound>moo</sound>se in the gallery, chewing the corner of the drawing.

眼.meaning: A <part>robot</part> loses its camera at the scrapyard, so it screws in a big glass <part>eye</part> it finds in a jar. The eye rolls round and round in the socket, blinking at pigeons and winking at the bin lorry. The robot loves its new <kanji>eyeball</kanji>.
眼.on: Each morning it wipes the green <sound>gun</sound>k off with an oily rag.
眼.kun: It sips oil from a <sound>mu</sound>g, munches <sound>na</sound>an and stares at a <sound>ko</sound>ala all day.

薄.meaning: After a game of <part>water polo</part>, the team tops up the lemonade jug with pool water, then the goalie stirs it with a fistful of <part>grass</part> 'for colour'. It tastes of chlorine and lawn and almost no lemon. It's the most <kanji>dilute</kanji> drink in town.
薄.on: Someone drops in one sad <sound>huc</sound>kleberry to help.
薄.kun: It's thinner than the broth on <sound>u</sound>don and greyer than <sound>soo</sound>t.

肥.meaning: A lazy farmer drags his <part>bed</part> out into the cabbage patch and sleeps there, snoring under the <part>moon</part>. His cows wander round him every night, and by spring the cabbages are the size of armchairs. Cow pats make great <kanji>fertilizer</kanji>.
肥.on: One morning he hops out of bed and his <sound>hee</sound>l sinks right into it.
肥.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala naps on a giant cabbage, and both keep getting fatter.

踏.meaning: The <part>sun</part> has baked the beach path so hot it burns toes, so a lifeguard sets buckets of <part>water</part> along it. Each <part>foot</part> goes splash, hiss, splash. Nobody walks; they hop from bucket to bucket, one cool <kanji>step</kanji> at a time.
踏.on: One man misses a bucket and stubs his <sound>toe</sound> on the rim.
踏.kun: He hops off to sulk on a beach <sound>fu</sound>ton in the shade.

紀.meaning: A wise <part>cobra</part> keeps the village's history by tying a knot in a long <part>thread</part> for every big event: a flood, a wedding, the day the goat ate the mayor's hat. Coiled in its basket, the thread is now miles long. Each knot is a line in the town's <kanji>chronicle</kanji>.
紀.on: The basket is locked with a brass <sound>key</sound> that the cobra keeps under its tongue.

酔.meaning: A miner lights a stick of <part>dynamite</part> beside the <part>signpost</part> at the crossroads. Boom: its arms spin and point every which way, up, down and sideways, and the post sways and hiccups. It looks completely <kanji>drunk</kanji>.
酔.on: Travellers argue about which arm points to the <sound>swee</sound>t shop.
酔.kun: A dizzy hiker leans on it, feeling sick, and spills <sound>yo</sound>gurt down his front.

沿.meaning: A lost duckling can't find the pond, so it trails the <part>water drops</part> leaking from a <part>funnel</part> strapped to a farmer's tractor. Drip, waddle, drip, waddle, across three fields and a car park. It has learned to <kanji>follow along</kanji>.
沿.on: The tractor's <sound>en</sound>gine puffs out smoke rings to keep it on track.
沿.kun: At the end of the trail, it flops onto a <sound>so</sound>fa beside the farmer.

州.meaning: A <part>river</part> splits into three streams, and a <part>dot</part> of an island sits in each gap. The islanders hold a vote, sew a flag with three blobs on it and print their own stamps. They're now their very own <kanji>state</kanji>.
州.on: Their parliament meets inside a giant <sound>shoe</sound> moored between the islands.
州.kun: The smallest island is just a <sound>soo</sound>ty heap of sand: a sandbank.

欧.meaning: A tour guide drags her group through every <part>ward</part> of every old city on the map: ten countries in ten days, cathedral, museum, castle, repeat. On day nine the whole bus lets out one giant <part>yawn</part>. That's a coach trip round <kanji>Europe</kanji>.
欧.on: They nap under a huge <sound>oa</sound>k in the last town square.
欧.kun: The guide slurps <sound>u</sound>don, climbs into a fountain <sound>tu</sound>b and belts out a tune to wake them: to sing.

招.meaning: A lonely lighthouse keeper ties a bell to the old <part>anchor</part> on the rocks and rings it at dusk, a <part>call</part> out over the waves. One by one the seals swim over, then a whale, then a lost tugboat. All he does is curl a finger to <kanji>beckon</kanji> them.
招.on: Then he puts on a <sound>show</sound>, juggling fish for his guests.
招.kun: He serves tea in a <sound>mu</sound>g and dries the seals off in a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t.

裂.meaning: Soldiers stand in a perfect <part>rank</part> for inspection, and the general bellows 'Chests out!' They puff up so hard that each tight <part>garment</part> rips down the back, one after another like dominoes. The whole row has <kanji>split</kanji>.
裂.on: The tailor gets a glass of <sound>rets</sound>ina for fixing them all.
裂.kun: Sewing them up takes all night and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

蒸.meaning: A frog builds a sauna in the marsh: <part>hot coals</part> at the bottom, <part>water</part> poured over them, <part>one</part> lily-pad bench and a roof of <part>grass</part>. When his glasses fog up, the job is <part>complete</part>. He sits there grinning in a cloud of <kanji>steam</kanji>.
蒸.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops out of its mother's pouch to join him on the bench.
蒸.kun: Soon a <sound>moo</sound>se squeezes in as well and fogs up the whole marsh.

才.meaning: A five-year-old builds a working submarine from a bathtub, a bicycle and an old <part>anchor</part> she found in the shed. It dives, it surfaces, it even makes toast. Scientists queue outside her house. She's a <kanji>genius</kanji>.
才.on: Her fuel is a jug of fizzy <sound>ci</sound>der, poured straight into the tank.

腰.meaning: Under a full <part>moon</part>, a werewolf feels a sudden <part>need</part> to dance. He puts his paws on his hips and wiggles, faster and faster, until his tail spins like a propeller. All that power comes from his <kanji>loins</kanji>.
腰.on: A <sound>yo</sound>-yo swings from his belt as he dances.
腰.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala joins in, wiggling her hips behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld.

漁.meaning: A <part>fish</part> sits on the riverbank in a tiny hat, dangling a worm on a line into the <part>water drops</part> of a rain puddle. It hasn't caught a person yet, but it's patient. Even fish like to go <kanji>fishing</kanji>.
漁.on: For lunch it gulps down one <sound>gyo</sound>za dumpling in a single quick bite.
漁.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' it sighs, scavenging the bank for a <sound>sa</sound>rdine: fishing for scraps.

律.meaning: A painter rides the <part>chairlift</part> up the mountain, and every time her chair passes a pole she dabs one stripe on the snow below with a long <part>brush</part>. Dab, swing, dab, swing, all day. By sunset the slope is striped in perfect time: pure <kanji>rhythm</kanji>.
律.on: She keeps a box of <sound>Ritz</sound> crackers on her lap and crunches one per stripe.

添.meaning: A cheeky man in a <part>tilted hat</part> moves his garden fence a little into his neighbour's yard every night, then sprinkles <part>water drops</part> and a <part>trickle</part> from his can so the new strip looks like his lawn. By summer the whole yard is <kanji>annexed</kanji>.
添.on: A <sound>ten</sound>or next door sings furious opera at him from the window.
添.kun: He even drags the neighbour's <sound>so</sound>fa over, as a little extra.

為.meaning: A tireless butler gets his to-do list: load the <part>staple</part> gun, <part>wrap</part> the parcels, rake the <part>hot coals</part>, put a <part>dot</part> over every i, and draw a <part>slash</part> through each job when it's finished. He never asks why. He just loves to <kanji>do</kanji>.
為.on: Last on the list: feed the <sound>ee</sound>l in the bathtub.
為.kun: He does it all for one <sound>ta</sound>co and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon: for his own benefit.

縁.meaning: A <part>pig</part> and a clothes <part>iron</part> meet at a laundry and can't stop smiling at each other. The pig ties a red <part>thread</part> from his curly tail to the iron's handle, and they waddle home together, steam puffing happily. Some pairs just have an <kanji>affinity</kanji>.
縁.on: On their first date, they ride in a car with a rumbling <sound>en</sound>gine.
縁.kun: They sit on the edge of a <sound>fu</sound>ton, watching a <sound>chee</sound>tah race past.
